sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. Petitioner in this writ petition seeks to assail the order dated 25th September, 2023 (Annexure-4)
passed by learned 3rd MACT- cum-Additional District Judge, Balasore in MAC No.193 of 2015,
whereby an application filed by the Petitioner to issue summon to the Investigating Officer of Betnoti P.S. Case No.125 of 2014 and call for the original case record in C.T. Case No.338 of 2014 from learned JMFC, Betnoti for just adjudication of the claim petition, has been rejected.

3. It is submitted by Mr. Dash, learned counsel for the Petitioner that M.A.C. Case No.193 of 2015 has been filed by the Opposite Party No.1-Claimant claiming compensation for the injury caused to her in a motor vehicle accident.
It is submitted that the Claimant-Opposite Party No.1 has stated in her petition that on the ill fated day, i.e., on 8th May, 2014, at about 9 P.M., the injured, namely,

Opposite Party No.1 was proceeding from medical quarter towards Betnoti CHC on NH-5, by walking on the extreme left side and when the Petitioner was about to reach the Betnoti Hospital, a Bajaj Allianz Insurance Corporation vs Binapani Sahoo And Another .... sentences.text: 1 motor cycle bearing Registration NO.OD-01-C-1917 (motor cycle) Designation: Junior Stenographer Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Date: 19-Jan-2024 13:19:06 came in a rash and negligent manner from Baripada side and dashed the Petitioner from her back side causing bodily injury to the Opposite Party No.1.
It is also stated that she was admitted to the Hospital and was discharged on 16th June, 2014, but the FIR was lodged belatedly on 18th July, 2014 involving the present motor cycle.

To the contrary, on the next date of accident, the matter was published in a newspaper in which it has been stated that an Indigo CS Car coming from the Balasore side, hit the Opposite Party No.1 and fled away.
It was a case of hit and run.

On the basis of the delayed FIR,
Betnoti PS Case No.125 of 2014 was registered and the investigation was taken up.
Charge sheet has already submitted against the person who was driving the motor cycle.

In recent days, fake claim cases are being filed and Hon'ble Supreme Court has also expressed its concern on the same in the case of Safiq Ahmad vrs. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd. and others (in special leave to Appeal(c) CC No.23628 of 2016).

It is also submitted that the size and scale of the crime goes far beyond the present case.
50. Therefore, considering the scale, magnitude and complexity of the crime, this Court is of the opinion that the State police is not in a position to carry out a fair and truthful investigation.
The CBI is well equipped with the requisite skill to unearth the conspiracy and money trailing aspect of the crime.

Therefore, this Court directs that the aforesaid cases be handed over to the CBI for investigation in the interest of justice in exercise of its inherent powers and in the spirit of the apex Court's judgment in Safiq Ahmad v. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra)."

He also relied upon the observation made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vrs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 Supreme Court Cases 343, wherein it is observed as under:
"16.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vrs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 Supreme Court Cases 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered in regard to the injuries and their effect, in particular, the extent of permanent disability.

Sections 168 and 169 of the Act make it evident that the Tribunal does not function as a neutral umpire as in a civil suit, but as an active explorer and seeker of truth who is required to "hold an enquiry into the claim" for determining the "just compensation".
The Tribunal should therefore take an active role to ascertain the true and correct position so that it can assess the "just compensation"."

2 5. He, therefore submits that the Claims Tribunal should not be a mute spectator to the fake cases filed and should act as an explorer and seeker of truth.
In the instant case, if the Investigating Officer of Betnoti PS Case No.125 of 2014 is summoned, the truth will come out.
Likewise, the case record of CT Case No.338 of 2014 will also reveal the truth.
In view of the above, the Petitioner filed an application (Annexure-3) to summon the Investigating Officer in Betnoti Case No.125 of 2014 for revealing the truth.
CT Case No.338 of 2014 from the Court of learned JMFC, Betnoti is also required to be called for that purpose.
The said application has been rejected by a cryptic order.
Hence, this writ petition has been filed.
6. It is submitted that learned Tribunal has not taken into consideration the grounds taken by the Petitioner-Insurance Company in the petition under Annexure-3.
Hence, the impugned order is not sustainable and is liable to be set aside.

Designation: Junior Stenographer Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Date:
19-Jan-2024 13:19:06 7.

Considering the submission made by Mr. Dash, learned counsel for the Petitioner and on perusal of the record, it appears that the certified copy of the FIR, Final Form and seizure list etc. have already been marked as Exhibits in the Claim Case (MAC Case No.193 of 2015).
8.

When the relevant documents and the final report have already been marked as exhibit in the Claim Case pending before the Claims Tribunal, this Court finds no reason to summon the Investigating Officer for his examination.
For that reason, original case record of C.T. Case No.338 of 2014 is also not required to be called for from the Court of learned JMFC, Betnoti.
Truth will come out from the record available before the Court.
It also appears that the matter is posted for adducing evidence on behalf of the Opposite Party No.2.
Thus, they are at liberty to adduce evidence in support of their case to prove that the Claimant-Opposite Party No.1 is not entitled to any compensation.
9. Although not in two many words, learned Claims Tribunal has spelt out the reasons for rejecting the petition under Annexure-3 and I find no infirmity in the said order.
10. Accordingly, the writ petition, being devoid of any merit, stands dismissed.

Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
 (K.R. Mohapatra)
